title: Numeric grounding of model rationales
why: Checking generated answers against their source data is the cheapest first line of LLM evaluation, before any LLM-as-judge (docs/SOURCES.md, lab sources).
notes: Every stored live rationale and key factor with a stored morning context (350 rationales; 1008 forecasts in the ledger).
Trivial numbers (small integers, years, dates) are ignored. A number counts as in the prompt if it equals one in the question, the rule or the context within its rounding or 1%.
limits: Not in the prompt is an upper bound on invented figures: a model can compute things (a weekly mean of seven values, for example) that are legitimate but not literally in the prompt.
The agents also read tool results (series, base rates, retrieval) that are not part of the stored morning context, so their share is overstated here.
It does not judge whether the reasoning is good, only whether the figures it quotes can be traced.
Small sample: the live record is a few days old; the numbers will move.
